newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK interbank market quiet, awaiting U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: HK interbank market quiet, awaiting U.S. data.

text.p: Hong Kong interbank market rates were unchanged on Friday awaiting economic data from the United States, dealers said.
The overnight ended unchanged at 5-1/8 percent while three month money finished at 5-1/2 7/16 percent, also unchanged.
"There is no change to the market, everyone is looking at the PPI (producer price index). If it's positive, term money demand would move up," a dealer with a foreign bank said.
Financial markets are awaiting U.S. September PPI data to be released later on Friday for clues on future U.S. interest rate policy.
Demand for government paper cooled in line with the overnight drop in U.S. Treasuries on renewed inflation fears.

Yields of seven-year Exchange Fund notes rose to 7.42 percent versus 7.38 percent on Thursday, while five year finished at 7.06 percent against 7.03 percent and three-year notes yields rose to 6.48 percent versus 6.41 percent.
The one-week Exchange Fund bill yield was unchanged at 4.80 percent.
